beats.caption: OneCare — clinician walkthrough
beats.narration: This is the clinician side of OneCare: a light surface for following patients between visits, without buying another electronic record system.

beats.caption: Sign-up, profile, BAA
beats.narration: Clinicians sign up, complete a profile with title, specialty, licence and country, and sign the business associate agreement before any patient data is exposed. Sessions time out after thirty minutes of genuine inactivity.

beats.caption: Today — one triage inbox
beats.narration: Today is one unified inbox, ordered by urgency: vital alerts, unread patient messages, guidance awaiting a reply, and open practice tasks. Everything is actionable in place — there is no separate alerts screen to check.

beats.caption: Work the inbox in place
beats.narration: You clear the list from the top down. Each row carries enough context to decide, and opens the patient only when you actually need the chart.

beats.caption: Patients — paginated and searchable
beats.narration: Patients is a simple paginated, searchable list. Nothing dense at list level: connected patients who granted you a private share, institution patients you've been assigned, and managed records for patients with no OneCare account.

beats.caption: Patient detail
beats.narration: Open a patient and you get medications, vitals, documents, guidance, encounters and internal notes — limited strictly to the categories that patient chose to share with you.

beats.caption: Vitals with provenance
beats.narration: Vitals arrive with their source attached, so you can tell a home reading from a clinic reading from an imported one before you act on a trend.

beats.caption: Medications and documents
beats.narration: Medications show what the patient is actually taking, not what was prescribed at discharge. Shared documents sit alongside, with AI summaries you can skim before the consultation.

beats.caption: Guidance the patient can answer
beats.narration: Guidance is structured instruction with a status the patient can respond to, rather than a message that disappears into a thread. Templates and specialty packs make the common cases a few clicks.

beats.caption: Messages
beats.narration: Messages are threaded per patient with attachments, and stay preserved for the record once a relationship ends.

beats.caption: Dictations and scribe
beats.narration: Dictations and scribe take a recording or an upload, return a transcript, then draft a SOAP note against an encounter. You edit and sign it — nothing is filed unsigned.

beats.caption: Clinical templates
beats.narration: Templates are reusable guidance and visit structures held at practice level, so a team writes the same instruction the same way every time.

beats.caption: Propose, approve, apply
beats.narration: The clinician assistant reads only what you can already read, and works in one direction: it proposes, you approve, then it applies and writes the action to the log. It never writes first, never prescribes, and cannot touch a patient outside your access.

beats.caption: Tasks and encounters
beats.narration: Practice work items carry an assignee, a due date and a status. Encounters are the clinical unit — type, time, participants, SOAP content and sign-off.

beats.caption: Team and roles
beats.narration: Team is where you invite members and set roles — owner, admin, provider, nurse, front desk, billing, read only — and remove people who leave. Cards appear only for the capabilities a member actually has, so a solo clinician never sees enterprise clutter.

beats.caption: Institution patients and hospital code
beats.narration: Institution patients are those who shared with the hospital rather than one clinician; consent and assignment are separate, so sharing with a hospital never exposes a chart to everyone in it. The hospital code is the short code patients type to connect.

beats.caption: Storage and subscription
beats.narration: Storage and durability show pooled usage against the tenant allowance, with packs to upgrade, and the subscription, EHR connections and branding sit alongside. Practice is where the practice is run — Settings is only where it's configured.

beats.caption: Bulk onboarding
beats.narration: Managed records can be created one at a time or imported from a spreadsheet, with duplicate detection and an error file back so a bad row never silently disappears.

beats.caption: Audit trail
beats.narration: Audit records who accessed which patient and when, exportable as a one-click compliance pack. Patients see the same trail from their side — the transparency runs both ways.

beats.caption: Institutions
beats.narration: For institutions, storage is pooled and billed at tenant level, and whitelabelling with a branded subdomain is coming soon. Write-back into connected electronic records stays deliberately out of scope until partner agreements exist — import and provenance are live today.

beats.caption: onecare.you
beats.narration: One inbox, one chart per patient, and a clear record of who did what. That's OneCare for clinicians.
